html.infoScreens:
Welcome

Before we begin, please make sure that:
  • You are comfortably seated
  • You have a mouse
  • You are ready to play in full-screen mode
  • You have about 40 minutes to spare

Information

1. Researcher responsible for the project
Marine VERNET, CNRS researcher
Lyon Neuroscience Research Center CRNL (INSERM U1028)
IMPACT team - 16 avenue du Doyen Lépine - 69676 Bron Cedex - FRANCE

2. Purpose of the research project
This research project aims to better understand how the brain of healthy adults works during a game where you have to beat your own scores and those of the computer.

3. Who can participate
You can participate in this study if you are 18 years old or older and in good health, with normal or corrected-to-normal vision, without a history of neurological or psychiatric disease, or known motor disorder.

4. What is expected of you
Your participation in this study consists of playing an online game. You will have to find an intruder among similar shapes and go click on it as fast as possible, in order to beat your own scores and those of the computer. You will also be asked to answer short questions about the experience, as well as a questionnaire at the end of the experience. The total duration of the study is estimated between 45 and 60 minutes.

5. Your rights to withdraw from research at any time
Your contribution to this research is voluntary and you must give your consent before participating. You are free to stop participating at any time. Your decision to participate, refuse to participate, or stop participating can be made at any time without justification and will have no effect on you. If you do not wish to participate, or if you wish to stop participating, you can simply close the browser window at any time. If you leave the game after starting it, your previously collected data will be saved.

6. Your rights to confidentiality and privacy
All data collected is completely anonymous and at no time it is possible to identify you. Furthermore, you will not be asked for any information that could reveal your identity.

7. Data retention
The data from this study will be kept for 5 years on the server of the Lyon Neuroscience Research Center, then archived on this same server for a period of 8 years before being destroyed. They may also be deposited on open access platforms.

8. Ethical aspects
This project received a favorable opinion from the Inserm Ethics Evaluation Committee (IRB00003888) on June 7th 2022.

9. Dissemination
The results of the study will be disseminated in scientific congresses, scientific journals and may be the subject of teaching and appear in educational materials.

10. Your rights to ask questions at any time
You can contact the scientific manager of this research at any time to request further information on the study (marine . vernet (at) inserm . fr).

Tutorial

The goal of this game is to spot the odd one out (your target) in a grid of geometrical shapes.

Tutorial

The odd one out not only has a different shape,
but also a unique color.

Tutorial

First, you must look for the odd one out without moving your mouse.

Tutorial

Once you have found it, you must press the spacebar to unlock the grid.

Tutorial

Once the grid is unlocked, you must move your mouse towards it in a single smooth motion, and then click on it.

Tutorial

To summarize, you must simply:

  1. Look for the odd one out
  2. Press the spacebar
  3. Move your mouse towards it in one smooth motion
  4. Click on it

Tutorial

Each trial will be considered successful only if you correctly follow these instructions. Otherwise, a window will interrupt the game and let you know how to correct yourself.

1. Whether or not I get to be a leader depends mostly on my ability.
2. To a great extent my life is controlled by accidental happenings.
3. I feel like what happens in my life is mostly determined by powerful people.
4. Whether or not I get into a car accident depends mostly on how good a driver I am.
5. When I make plans, I am almost certain to make them work.
6. Often there is no chance of protecting my personal interests from bad luck.
7. When I get what I want, it’s usually because I’m lucky.
8. Although I might have good ability, I will not be given leadership responsibility without appealing to those in positions of power.
9. How many friends I have depends on how nice a person I am.
10. I have often found that what is going to happen will happen.
11. My life is chiefly controlled by powerful others.
12. Whether or not I get into a car accident is mostly a matter of luck.
13. People like myself have very little chance of protecting our personal interests when they conflict with those of strong pressure groups.
14. It’s not always wise for me to plan too far ahead because many things turn out to be a matter of good or bad fortune.
15. Getting what I want requires pleasing those people above me.
16. Whether or not I get to be a leader depends on whether I’m lucky enough to be in the right place at the right time.
17. If important people were to decide they didn’t like me, I probably wouldn’t make many friends.
18. I can pretty much determine what will happen in my life.
19. I am usually able to protect my personal interests.
20. Whether or not I get into a car accident depends mostly on the other driver.
21. When I get what I want, it’s usually because I worked hard for it.
22. In order to have my plans work, I make sure that they fit in with the desires of people who have power over me.
23. My life is determined by my own actions.
